title: Imported: the theorems that deliver $2\pi$, and their hypotheses
subject: thermality
one_liner: Under the spectrum condition, covariance and locality, the modular flow of a wedge or half-sided algebra is the boost at rate $2\pi$, and a regular stationary quasi-free state at a bifurcate Killing horizon is KMS at $\kappa/2\pi$.

title: The blade basis persists under degeneracy
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: For any symmetric bilinear form on an $m$-dimensional real space, degenerate or not, the $2^m$ blades of any basis form a linear basis of $\Cl(W,B)$.

title: The blade basis persists under degeneracy (external ingredients)
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: The blade-basis fact draws on Chevalley's classical theory of Clifford algebras.

title: Minimal nondegenerate completion
subject: completion
one_liner: A real quadratic space with radical of dimension $r$ and nondegenerate part of signature $(p,q)$ has minimal nondegenerate completions of exactly $r$ extra dimensions, all of signature $(p+r,q+r)$ and unique up to an isometry fixing the space, so $\Cl(p,q,r)$ embeds in $\Cl(p+r,q+r)$, minimally among completion-induced embeddings.

title: The Witt extension theorem
subject: completion
one_liner: Over a field of characteristic not two, an isometry between arbitrary subspaces of two isometric nondegenerate quadratic spaces extends to an isometry of the whole spaces.

title: The Chevalley pairing
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The Chevalley pairing on the Fock module pairs the two chiralities perfectly, is antisymmetric, makes every vector self-transpose and is infinitesimally $\Spin$-invariant.

title: The chiral planes, and the summand spaces
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The two planes $\Som$, $\Spi$ of the conformal spinor space are the chiral doublets of the complexified Lorentz algebra, their tensor product is complexified Minkowski space, and each equivariant map from a direction and one plane to the other is unique up to scale.

title: The chirality split, and the ordering insensitivity of the ASD sector
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The complexified Lorentz algebra splits into commuting self-dual and anti-self-dual copies of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$, and ordering discrepancies within the anti-self-dual sector of the palatial algebra stay in that sector and never source the googly slot.

title: The Fock model of the complexified ascended algebra
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The exterior algebra on a maximal isotropic subspace, with wedge and contraction operators, is the unique irreducible module of the complexified Clifford algebra $\Cl(2,4)_\C$, and its even and odd halves are the two four-dimensional chiralities.

title: Imported: complete reducibility
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: Every finite-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ is a direct sum of irreducibles, and its decomposition into isotypic components is canonical.

title: Imported: the forced completion and its fibre quadric
subject: completion
one_liner: Division by a type-N zero divisor in $\Cl(1,3)$ has no element-level resolution, its unique minimal resolving completion is $\Cl(1,3) \hookrightarrow \Cl(2,4)$, and the resolving assignments lie on the null quadric of $\R^{2,4}$.

title: Imported: stabilisers in the flat model
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: In $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ the stabiliser of the null vector at infinity is the Poincar\'e algebra, the stabiliser of its ray is the eleven-dimensional maximal parabolic, and its nilradical is the translations, which are the no-go theorem's transvections.

title: Imported: the vacuum equations and the scale tractor
subject: einstein
one_liner: On the invertible region of a gravitational field on flat spacetime the vacuum equations are the parallelism of the scale tractor for the tractor gauge field, and a parallel section $(1, 0, \rho)$ is exactly an Einstein scale with $\Lambda = 6\rho$ and squared norm $\Lambda/3$.

title: The incidence relation is the chart
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The Pl\"ucker bivector of the incidence line of a map $A$ is exactly the completion's null point embedding $X(m(A))$, so Penrose's incidence relation is the completion's affine chart, with a determinant as its quadratic term.

title: Lorentzian duality is a complex structure
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: On $2$-forms of an oriented four-dimensional Lorentzian space the Hodge star squares to $-1$, with three-dimensional, mutually conjugate eigenspaces for the eigenvalues $\pm I_5$ of its complexification by the central pseudoscalar $I_5$ of the odd extension.

title: One statement in three languages
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: On the invertible region of a gravitational field on flat spacetime, the vacuum and Einstein equations are equivalent to covariant constancy of the infinity bivector of the conformal spinor space, which is simple exactly when the cosmological constant vanishes.

title: Skew lines, splittings, hyperbolic planes: one datum
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: An ordered pair of skew lines in the projective spinor space, a normalised splitting of the conformal spinor space into two planes and a normalised null pair in $V_\C$ determine one another, with the mixed slot equal to the orthogonal complement of the null pair.

title: The spin representation is $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The Clifford bivectors form $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)_\C$ and act on the conformal spinor space as an isomorphism onto $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$, so the spin group acts on $\CS$ as all of $SL(\CS)$, transitively on nonzero conformal spinors.

title: The spinor identification
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: There is a canonical $\Spin$-equivariant isomorphism from $V_\C$ to the bivectors of the conformal spinor space carrying the quadratic form to the wedge square, so null vectors are exactly the simple bivectors, that is, the lines of the projective spinor space.

title: Symmetrised quadratics of the palatial algebra
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The symmetrised quadratics of the palatial algebra realise $\mathfrak{gl}(4,\C)$ faithfully through commutators and equal the normal-ordered ones minus the central term $\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{tr}M$, a shift of $-2\hbar$ for the helicity generator.

title: Imported: the frozen point and its geometry
subject: dark-energy
one_liner: On the invertible region of a gravitational field on flat spacetime the Einstein condition makes the scale tractor parallel for the tractor connection, with $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, stabiliser $SO(1,4)$ or $SO(2,3)$, and $P_{ab} = (\Lambda/6)g_{ab}$.

title: Imported: the frozen point and its geometry (external ingredients)
subject: dark-energy
one_liner: The frozen-point fact takes its tractor connection and almost-Einstein scale tractor from Gover's work on almost-Einstein manifolds.

title: The Stelle-West vector of the frozen point
subject: dark-energy
one_liner: In the frozen point's scale, $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ is orthogonal to $I$ with $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ and $\nabla V = e$, and the tractor gauge field is $\Omega(a) + \hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/Q(V)$.

title: Full uniqueness, given the dynamics
subject: thermality
one_liner: Given the boost dynamics and $\beta$, the I-state is the unique $\tau$-KMS state of the boundary-mode algebra among all states.

title: Gibbs states are KMS, and conversely, in finite dimensions
subject: descent
one_liner: On a full matrix algebra with dynamics generated by a diagonal Hamiltonian, the Gibbs state at inverse temperature $\beta$ is KMS, and it is the unique KMS state at that $\beta$, degenerate spectrum included.

title: The I-state
subject: thermality
one_liner: At the Hawking temperature the Fermi-Dirac quasi-free state on the boundary-mode algebra is KMS for the boost dynamics, and it is the only quasi-free state that is, with gauge invariance and its symbol both forced.

title: The I-state on the continuum
subject: thermality
one_liner: On the continuum mode space at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, for any self-adjoint $h$, the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ is $\tau$-KMS and is the unique $\tau$-KMS state.

title: Imported: the algebra of the boundary modes is the CAR algebra
subject: tower
one_liner: For even transport charge the completed complexified limit of the tower is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$, with the adjoined null pairs as its mode operators, and the physical lineage, of charge six, is covered.

title: Imported: ideal-Fermi-gas uniqueness
subject: descent
one_liner: For free fermions with quasi-free dynamics the $\beta$-KMS state is unique and is the quasi-free state with Fermi-Dirac symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$.

title: Imported: KMS passes to inductive limits
subject: descent
one_liner: A state that is KMS at $\beta$ on each subalgebra of an increasing chain of dynamics-invariant subalgebras is KMS at $\beta$ on the closure of their union.

title: Imported: quasi-free KMS reduces to the two-point level
subject: descent
one_liner: A gauge-invariant quasi-free CAR state is KMS for quasi-free dynamics exactly when its two-point function satisfies the two-point KMS identity.

title: Imported: quasi-free states of the CAR algebra
subject: thermality
one_liner: Each symbol $0 \le A \le 1$ determines a unique gauge-invariant quasi-free state of the CAR algebra; quasi-free states are fixed by their symbol and pairing, and gauge invariance is the vanishing of the pairing.

title: KMS restricts to invariant subalgebras
subject: descent
one_liner: A KMS state restricts to a KMS state at the same inverse temperature on any unital subalgebra invariant under the dynamics.

title: Modular structure of the completed pair
subject: descent
one_liner: The completed pair's bivector $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*}$ is a unit boost whose rotor flow scales the pair with opposite weights, whose spectral projectors are the occupation projectors, and which is unique up to reparametrisation and orientation.

title: The boosts generate exactly the Levi factor
subject: einstein
one_liner: The three boosts generate exactly the six-dimensional Lorentz algebra $\Lambda^2 W \cong \mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, with no component outside it.

title: Covariant form of the vacuum equations
subject: einstein
one_liner: On the invertible region of a gravitational field on flat spacetime, the vacuum field equations hold exactly when the null scale tractor $\nInf$ of the derived metric is parallel for the tractor gauge field $\Omega_{T}$.

title: Imported: equivalence with the Einstein equations
subject: einstein
one_liner: Wherever $\hb$ is invertible, the GTG field equations are equivalent to Einstein's equations for the induced metric, and in vacuum to its Ricci-flatness.

title: Imported: the tractor connection
subject: einstein
one_liner: For a gravitational field on flat spacetime, the tractor bundle of its conformal class (the $\Cl(2,4)$ vectors $\sigma\nInf + \mu + \rho\nO$) carries a canonical metric-preserving connection, given in a chosen scale by an explicit formula involving the Schouten tensor.

title: Metric parallelism, and the trace of the Schouten condition
subject: einstein
one_liner: The tractor gauge field preserves the tractor metric, and a Schouten map proportional to the identity forces the factor to be $R/24$ and the field to be Einstein, so $\Sch = 0$ exactly when $\Ric = 0$.

title: Non-null stabilisers, and the section they act on
subject: einstein
one_liner: A non-null vector $I$ has the reductive ten-dimensional stabiliser $\mathfrak{so}(I^\perp)$, and its hyperplane section of the null quadric is de Sitter or anti-de Sitter space according to the sign of $Q(I)$.

title: $\Lambda \neq 0$: the scale tractor leaves the cone
subject: einstein
one_liner: For a gravitational field whose derived metric is Einstein with constant $\Lambda$, the section $\nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ is parallel, every parallel section $(1, 0, \rho)$ arises this way, and its squared norm is $\Lambda/3$.

title: The sign is fixed internally
subject: einstein
one_liner: Within the series' conventions, the sign of the Schouten term of the tractor gauge field is forced by requiring that $\Lambda > 0$ give the de Sitter section.

title: The stabiliser rotates from parabolic to reductive
subject: einstein
one_liner: The stabiliser of the frozen point is the Poincar\'e group for $\Lambda = 0$, the de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and the anti-de Sitter group $SO(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$.

title: Stabilisers in the flat model
subject: einstein
one_liner: In the flat model the stabiliser of the null vector $\nInf$ is the Poincar\'e algebra, that of its ray is the eleven-dimensional maximal parabolic, and the nilradical acts as translations through null shears.

title: The chart form of the spin isomorphism
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: In the conformal spinor chart, the dilation, the translations and the special conformal generators correspond to the grading element and to the maps $b_x: \Spi \to \Som$ and $c_x: \Som \to \Spi$ between the chiral halves.

title: The de Sitter scale and its frozen point
subject: dark-energy
one_liner: On flat spacetime de Sitter space is the gravitational field $\hb = \sigma$, $\sigma = 1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12$, with derived metric $\sigma^{-2}\eta$, and its frozen point is the unique constant vector $I_\Lambda = n_\infty + (\Lambda/6)n_0$, of squared norm $\Lambda/3$, which is the point at infinity $n_\infty$ at $\Lambda = 0$.

title: Imported: the flat model, the conformal spinor chart, and the infinity bivector
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: Imported: on the flat model the point embedding is null, $V_\C = \Lambda^2\CS$ with null meaning simple, $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS) \cong \so(\Lambda^2\CS, \varepsilon)$, and for $\Lambda = 0$ the infinity bivector is constant and simple.

title: Imported: flat model, conformal spinor chart and infinity bivector (external)
subject: conformal-spacetime
one_liner: The external ingredients of the flat-model fact: the conformal tractor dictionary of Bailey, Eastwood and Gover, and classical spinor material from Penrose and Rindler and from Hughston.

title: Imported: the frozen point and the tractor connection
subject: einstein
one_liner: For a vacuum Einstein field on flat spacetime the tractor gauge field has a parallel frozen point $I = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ of squared norm $\Lambda/3$, with stabiliser $SO(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$.

title: Imported: the Thomas operator
subject: einstein
one_liner: The Thomas operator sends a weight-$w$ density to a conformally invariant tractor, and at $w = 1$ it produces the scale tractor, which is the frozen point for an Einstein scale.

title: The centre
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: For $n \geq 1$ the centre of $\Cl(p,q)$ is $\R \cdot 1$ when $n$ is even and $\R \cdot 1 \oplus \R \cdot \omega$ when $n$ is odd.

title: The commutation rule
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: If $x$ lies in the subalgebra generated by vectors orthogonal to $v$, then $v x = \hat{x} v$ and $x v = v \hat{x}$.

title: The sign of $\omega^2$
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: The pseudoscalar of $\Cl(p,q)$ satisfies $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{(p-q)(p-q-1)/2}$, so $\omega^{2} = +1$ exactly when $p - q \equiv 0$ or $1 \pmod 4$.

title: Splitting along a hyperbolic plane
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: Along a hyperbolic plane spanned by a null pair $(v, w_0)$, every element of $\Cl(H_0 \perp U')$ expands uniquely as $\alpha + v\beta + w_0\gamma + v w_0\delta$ with coefficients in $\Cl(U')$, and left multiplication by $v$ is injective on $\Cl(U')$.

title: Blade basis, degenerate forms included
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: For any symmetric bilinear form, degenerate or not, and any basis, the $2^n$ blades form a basis of the Clifford algebra, with structure constants polynomial in the entries of the form.

title: $\kappa = 1/4M$, computed
subject: thermality
one_liner: For the Schwarzschild field on flat spacetime the redshifted acceleration of static observers, $v = K/\sqrt f$, is $f'(r)/2$, so the surface gravity is $\kappa = 1/4M$.

title: The Euclidean section, and its period
subject: thermality
one_liner: The Euclidean section of the Schwarzschild field is smooth at its tip, the Euclidean counterpart of the bifurcation sphere, if and only if imaginary Killing time has period $p = 2\pi/\kappa = 8\pi M$; any other period leaves a conical point of total angle $\kappa p$.

title: Imported: surface gravity as redshifted acceleration
subject: thermality
one_liner: For a static Killing horizon, the surface gravity, $(K \cdot D)K = \kappa K$ on the horizon locus, equals the horizon limit of the redshift-weighted proper acceleration of static observers.

title: KMS uniqueness at a factor
subject: descent
one_liner: On a matrix factor, for each nonzero inverse temperature the only KMS state of an inner flow is the Gibbs state of its generator.

title: Modular theory of a matrix factor, proved outright
subject: descent
one_liner: For a full matrix algebra with a cyclic separating vector, the modular operator, modular conjugation and modular flow are computed explicitly, and the state is KMS for that flow.

title: Rate rigidity: the temperature is not algebra intrinsic
subject: thermality
one_liner: Automorphisms of the single-mode algebra that intertwine the boost's phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the atom's complex unit, move its KMS states only by $\beta \mapsto \pm\beta$, so the value of the temperature depends on a parametrisation of the flow that the algebra does not supply.

title: Exponentials of bivectors with scalar square
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: If $A^{2} = \lambda \in \R$ then $e^{A}$ is $\cos\theta + \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}A$, $\cosh\theta + \frac{\sinh\theta}{\theta}A$ or $1 + A$, a rotor with $e^{A}\widetilde{e^{A}} = 1$.

sources.locator: Ch. 4 (foundations of geometric algebra: rotors, versors)
Ch. 3 (versors, rotors and the bivector algebra)

title: Bivectors form the Lie algebra of the orthogonal group
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl^{2}$ is closed under $A \times C = \langle AC \rangle_2$, acts skew-adjointly on $V$ by $A \times x = \langle Ax \rangle_1$, and is isomorphic to $\so(V,Q)$ when $Q$ is nondegenerate.

sources.locator: Ch. 4 (foundations of geometric algebra: rotors, versors)
Ch. 3 (versors, rotors and the bivector algebra)

title: The blade basis, degenerate forms included
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: For any basis of $V$ the $2^{n}$ increasing products $e_I$ form a basis of $\Cl(V, Q)$, degenerate forms included; so $V \hookrightarrow \Cl(V, Q)$.

sources.locator: Ch. II (the Clifford algebra of a quadratic space)

title: The invariant pairing on spinors
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\beta(x, y) = \operatorname{top}(\tau x \wedge y)$ is nondegenerate on $\Lambda W$, has symmetry $(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$, and satisfies $\beta(ax, y) = \beta(x, \tilde{a}y)$, so $\tilde{R}R = 1$ preserves it.

sources.locator: Ch. II and III (spinors, pure spinors)

title: Cl(1,1) and Cl(2,0) are the real 2x2 matrices
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl(H) \cong \Mat_2(\R)$ for a hyperbolic plane, since $uw, u, w, wu$ are matrix units of $\Cl(H)$ for a hyperbolic pair $(u, w)$; also $\Cl(2,0) \cong \Mat_2(\R)$.

sources.locator: Ch. V (Clifford algebras: the tensor product rules)

title: The complex Clifford algebra, its classification modulo 2, its Fock model and its pairing
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl(V_\C)$ has a blade basis and only depends on $n$: $\Cl_{2k}(\C) \cong \End(\Lambda W) \cong \Mat_{2^{k}}(\C)$ on any maximal totally null $W$, $\Cl_{2k+1}(\C) \cong \Mat_{2^{k}}(\C)^{\oplus 2}$; $\operatorname{top}(\tau x \wedge y)$ is a $\C$-bilinear invariant pairing, antisymmetric for $k = 3$.

sources.locator: Ch. II and III (Clifford algebras over a field; spinors, pure spinors)
Ch. I, Sections 4 and 5 (complex Clifford algebras and their representations)

title: Complexification, and the odd-dimensional split
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl(V) \otimes \C \cong \Cl_n(\C)$, a complex matrix algebra (doubled for odd $n$); for odd $n$, $\Cl \cong \Cl^{+} \oplus \Cl^{+}$ if $\omega^{2} = 1$ and $\Cl \cong \Cl^{+} \otimes \C$ if $\omega^{2} = -1$.

sources.locator: Ch. V (Clifford algebras: the tensor product rules)

title: The even subalgebra is a Clifford algebra one dimension down
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: For $Q(e) = s \ne 0$, $u \mapsto ue$ gives $\Cl(e^{\perp}, -sQ) \cong \Cl^{+}(V, Q)$; so $\Cl^{+}(p,q,r) \cong \Cl(p,q{-}1,r)$ for $q \ge 1$ and $\Cl^{+}(p,q,r) \cong \Cl(q,p{-}1,r)$ for $p \ge 1$.

sources.locator: Ch. V (Clifford algebras: the tensor product rules)

title: The Clifford algebra exists and is unique
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl(V, Q) = T(V)/\langle v \otimes v - Q(v) \rangle$ exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism; the wedge-plus-contraction operators on $\Lambda V$ give a concrete representation.

sources.locator: Ch. II (the Clifford algebra of a quadratic space)

title: The outer product is the exterior algebra
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $(\Cl(V, Q), \wedge) \cong (\Lambda V, \wedge)$ as graded algebras, by the identity on $V$; $v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge v_k = [v_1, \dots, v_k]$ and $\wedge$ does not depend on $Q$.

sources.locator: Ch. II (the Clifford algebra of a quadratic space)

title: The Fock representation, and the Fock space as a minimal left ideal
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl(\R^{k,k}) \cong \End(\Lambda W)$ by wedge and contraction, and the Fock space is the minimal left ideal $\Cl\, f$ of the vacuum idempotent $f = \prod_i v_i w_i$.

sources.locator: Ch. II and III (spinors, pure spinors)

title: Isometries extend to algebra homomorphisms
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: An isometry $f$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\Cl(f)$, injective when $f$ is; $\mathrm{O}(V, Q)$ acts by automorphisms.

sources.locator: Ch. II (the Clifford algebra of a quadratic space)

title: The grade decomposition
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: In an orthogonal basis $\Cl^{k} = \operatorname{span}\{e_I : |I| = k\}$, so $\Cl = \bigoplus_k \Cl^{k}$ with $\dim \Cl^{k} = \binom{n}{k}$, independently of the basis.

sources.locator: Ch. II (the Clifford algebra of a quadratic space)

title: Which vectors and versors are invertible
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $v$ is invertible iff $Q(v) \ne 0$, with $v^{-1} = v/Q(v)$; a versor $g = u_1 \cdots u_k$ has $g\tilde{g} = \prod Q(u_i)$.

sources.locator: Ch. 4 (foundations of geometric algebra: rotors, versors)

title: The three involutions on each grade
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: On $\Cl^{k}$: $\hat{x} = (-1)^{k}x$, $\tilde{x} = (-1)^{k(k-1)/2}x$, $\bar{x} = (-1)^{k(k+1)/2}x$; the first is an automorphism, the others anti-automorphisms.

title: Matrix units give a matrix algebra over the corner
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: A full $m \times m$ system of matrix units $E_{ij}$ in $A$ gives $A \cong \Mat_m(E_{11} A E_{11})$ via $b \mapsto (E_{1i} b E_{j1})$; e.g. $\Cl(1,1) \cong \Mat_2(\R)$.

sources.locator: matrix rings, idempotents and Morita theory

title: An algebra and its matrix amplification
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Zc(\Mat_m(A)) = \Zc(A)$, the ideals of $\Mat_m(A)$ are $\Mat_m(I)$, and $A$ and $\Mat_m(A)$ have equivalent module categories.

sources.locator: matrix rings, idempotents and Morita theory

title: Orthogonal vectors anticommute
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $uv = -vu$ iff $B(u,v) = 0$; in an orthogonal basis $e_I e_J = \pm \prod_{I \cap J} Q(e_i)\; e_{I \triangle J}$ with the sorting sign.

title: Periodicity and the table of real Clifford algebras
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1) \cong \Mat_2(\Cl(p,q))$, $\Cl(p{+}8,q) \cong \Cl(p,q{+}8) \cong \Mat_{16}(\Cl(p,q))$, and the table for $k \le 8$ gives every $\Cl(p,q)$ by $p - q \bmod 8$.

sources.locator: the tables of real Clifford algebras

title: Polarisation
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: The polar form is symmetric with $B(v,v) = Q(v)$, every symmetric bilinear form arises this way, and in a basis $Q(x) = x^{\mathsf T} G x$.

sources.locator: Ch. I and II (quadratic forms; the real case)

title: A vector times a multivector
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $aX = a \rfloor X + a \wedge X$ with $a \rfloor X = \tfrac12(aX - \hat{X}a)$ and $a \wedge X = \tfrac12(aX + \hat{X}a)$.

title: How the pseudoscalar commutes
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $I X_k = (-1)^{k(n-1)} X_k I$; $I\tilde{I} = \prod_i Q(e_i)$, and $I^{2} = 0$ in a degenerate algebra.

title: Reflection in a non-null vector
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: For $Q(u) \ne 0$, $x \mapsto -uxu^{-1} = x - 2\frac{B(x,u)}{Q(u)}u$ is the reflection in $u^{\perp}$: an involutive isometry of determinant $-1$ fixing $\operatorname{rad} V$.

sources.locator: Ch. 4 (foundations of geometric algebra: rotors, versors)
Ch. 3 (versors, rotors and the bivector algebra)

title: The tensor product rules
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: For $W$ even-dimensional with $\omega_W^{2} = \epsilon$, $\Cl(V \perp W, \epsilon Q \oplus Q_W) \cong \Cl(V) \otimes \Cl(W)$; hence $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1) \cong \Mat_2(\Cl(p,q))$, $\Cl(q{+}2,p) \cong \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Cl(2,0)$, $\Cl(q,p{+}2) \cong \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Cl(0,2)$.

sources.locator: Ch. V (Clifford algebras: the tensor product rules)

title: The product of two vectors
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $v^{2} = Q(v)$ and $uv + vu = 2B(u, v)$, so $uv = B(u, v) + \tfrac12(uv - vu)$.

title: Null pairs satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: For a Witt basis ($B(v_i,v_j) = B(w_i,w_j) = 0$, $B(v_i,w_j) = \tfrac12\delta_{ij}$), $\{v_i,v_j\} = \{w_i,w_j\} = 0$ and $\{v_i,w_j\} = \delta_{ij}$ in $\Cl(V,Q)$.

sources.locator: Ch. II and III (spinors, pure spinors)

title: Hyperbolic pairs and the Witt decomposition
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: A null vector in a nondegenerate plane has a unique hyperbolic partner, and $V = H_1 \perp \dots \perp H_{\min(p,q)} \perp A \perp \operatorname{rad} V$ with $A$ definite; maximal totally null subspaces have dimension $\min(p,q) + r$.

sources.locator: Ch. I (hyperbolic planes, the Witt decomposition, Witt's theorems)

title: The even subalgebra and the Z2 grading
subject: standard-algebra
one_liner: $\Cl = \Cl^{+} \oplus \Cl^{-}$ is a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading, $\dim \Cl^{+} = 2^{n-1}$, and $\Cl^{j}\Cl^{k}$ has grades $|j-k|, |j-k|+2, \dots, j+k$.

title: Completion recovers the real Clifford algebras; Sylvester's law of inertia in GA
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: If the coefficients form a complete ordered field (premise (F4)), every real quadratic space has an anticommuting basis of squares $1, -1, 0$ with invariant counts (Sylvester, derived in GA; Euclidean suffices) and every real Clifford algebra is $\Cl_{\Q}(p,q,r) \otimes \R$, inside $\Cl_{\Q}(p{+}r,q{+}r) \otimes \R$; over $\Q$ square classes remain ($\langle 2, 3\rangle$ is a division algebra).

title: Premise (F4): the coefficients are completed to a complete ordered field
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: Premise (F4): the rational coefficients are extended to a complete ordered field $\R$ (an ordered field in which every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound), the field of the store's real quadratic spaces and Clifford algebras; a mathematical primitive, not a physical one.

title: The cosmological horizon's boost is the frozen point's time translation
subject: dark-energy
one_liner: The static time of de Sitter space is the bivector $B_{\Lambda} = e_{0}\wedge W$ in the frozen point's stabiliser, with $B_{\Lambda}^{2} = \kappa_{\Lambda}^{2} = Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$: the cosmological horizon's surface gravity squared is the frozen point's norm.

title: Imported: the dictionary between Gauge Theory Gravity and curved-spacetime language
subject: einstein
one_liner: On the invertible region, tangent vectors are $\hb^{-1}(a)$, the Levi-Civita derivative is $D_a$, geodesics have $D$-parallel velocity, and the Riemann, Ricci, Schouten and Weyl tensors and Killing fields are read from the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B)$ and $D$.

title: Imported: Powers-Stormer quasi-equivalence, Araki purity and Takesaki disjointness
subject: thermality
one_liner: Gauge-invariant quasi-free CAR states $\omega_{A}$, $\omega_{B}$ are factor states, quasi-equivalent iff $A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}$ and $(1 - A)^{1/2} - (1 - B)^{1/2}$ are Hilbert-Schmidt and otherwise disjoint, and pure iff $A$ is a projection (Araki); $\|A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}\|_{2}^{2} \le \|A - B\|_{1}$ for bounded positive $A$, $B$ (Powers-Størmer); KMS states at different temperatures are disjoint when one induces a type III algebra (Takesaki).

title: Local boost temperature is local regularity
subject: einstein
one_liner: For any patch carrying modes on which the local boost acts by phases (assumed), clause (iii) of version 1 of (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), read on the patch's whole mode algebra, is equivalent to its clause (ii) (KMS at $\beta$ iff faithful with modular group the boost at $-\beta s$, on every window), and both together are (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), the joint KMS condition of the I-state for the local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$, a new premise stronger than the local form of (R); derived is only the geometric half, that this period is where the local boost's Euclidean section is regular for every field strength at leading order, giving $T = a/2\pi$ up to a relative correction $-\tfrac32k\rho^{2} + O(\rho^{3})$.

title: Premise (N$_{+}$): the null ground state on horizon generators
subject: thermality
one_liner: Premise (N$_{+}$): on the continuum of a horizon's null generators (eternal hole, an idealisation when $\Lambda > 0$, de Sitter, local Rindler horizons, the last at leading order where the gravitational field strength is nonzero, argued; holes formed by collapse through its short-distance form on the ingoing sheet, given J3) the modes are in a gauge-invariant quasi-free ground state for the affine null translations, acting on the fields by parallel transport (the orientation of the unit $I_{4}$ relative to time assumed); it delivers the continuum restatements of (R), (R$_{\Lambda}$), (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and the joint KMS part of (Q), with the thermal import moved to regularity across the bifurcation surface (within the stationary class, its local form there); on the Minkowski local horizons, and on de Sitter horizons for conformally invariant fields, it is the choice of the twistor attachment's vacuum, and only at the eternal hole is its positivity assumed.

title: The null vacuum on a horizon generator
subject: thermality
one_liner: On the continuum mode space of a null generator, the gauge-invariant quasi-free ground states of the affine null translations are exactly the filled sea $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$, $P = I_{4}\,d/du$, with kernel $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$; the weight-$\tfrac12$ boost dilates the translations, and on either half-generator the null vacuum is the continuum I-state at rapidity period exactly $2\pi$ for the boost future-directed there, with no premise assumed.

title: A point-spectrum boost admits no half-sided translations
subject: thermality
one_liner: A boost that acts by phases on a generating set of modes (pure point spectrum: windows, the countable mode space, the array of (Q)) dilates no strongly continuous translation group, even on the GNS space of a KMS state, so the Borchers and Bisognano-Wichmann route to (R) must be posed on the continuum mode space.

title: Premise (F2): minimal non-commutativity
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: Premise (F2): the directions $e_{1}, \dots, e_{n}$ and a central bit $c$ generate a group $G$ with $c^{2} = 1$, $G/\langle c\rangle = \mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$ via $S \mapsto e_{S}$, and $e_{i}e_{j} = c\,e_{j}e_{i} \ne e_{j}e_{i}$ for $i \ne j$; the signature, which directions square to $c$, is left free.

title: Premise (F3): superposition over the integers
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: Premise (F3): configurations superpose with integer coefficients and the sign bit acting as $-1$, so the algebra of the foundation is $\Z[G]/(c + 1)$; the integers, not a field, are the assumed coefficients.

title: Premise (F1): the bit
subject: clifford-structure
one_liner: Premise (F1): the foundation's primitive is one distinction, the two-element field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$ ($1 + 1 = 0$), repeated independently, so the configurations of $n$ distinctions are $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$ under symmetric difference; a mathematical choice with no sign, order or geometry.

title: The algebraic limit, even charge
subject: tower
one_liner: For even charge the algebraic direct limit of the tower is canonically $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$, equivalently the Clifford algebra of $\R^{p,q} \perp H_1 \perp H_2 \perp \cdots$.

title: The CAR limit, even charge
subject: tower
one_liner: For $p - q$ even, the C*-completion of the complexified tower limit is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$, with the adjoined null vectors as the fermionic mode operators.

title: Commuting copies
subject: tower
one_liner: Each floor $\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ of the tower is canonically a twisted copy of $\Cl(p,q)$ tensored with $\Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, that is $\Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$.

title: Compatibility: the connecting maps, transported
subject: tower
one_liner: For even charge the transported tower embedding is block doubling followed by conjugation by the invertible corrector $V_k = \operatorname{diag}(u_A \otimes 1_{2^k},\ 1_A \otimes \overline\Omega_k)$, which splits the correction across the two tensor legs.

title: Fock module; one qubit per rung
subject: tower
one_liner: The Chevalley action makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$ an irreducible $2^k$-dimensional module for $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ with a cyclic vacuum, and each rung doubles it.

title: Glimm's classification, and CAR uniqueness
subject: tower
one_liner: The completion of a unital chain of matrix algebras $\Mat_{2^k}(\C)$ is the unique $2^\infty$ UHF algebra, and the CAR algebra over $\ell^2$ is canonically determined by its relations and isomorphic to it.

title: The grade twist, and when it is inner
subject: tower
one_liner: The tower embedding is a diagonal twisted by the grade involution, which is inner, implemented by the ground volume element, when $p - q$ is even, and outer when $p - q$ is odd.

title: The ladder pairs satisfy the CAR, as vectors
subject: tower
one_liner: In the $k$-th tower algebra the $k$ adjoined null pairs satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of $k$ fermionic modes exactly, as vectors, and each new rung adds one mode without altering the existing relations.

title: The *-structure of the tower, and its C*-norms
subject: tower
one_liner: Each complexified floor of the tower has a unique frame-adapted *-structure respected by all the tower's maps and correctors, and for $p - q$ even each floor is a full complex matrix algebra, so the floors and their union carry unique C*-norms.

title: Volume elements of the planes
subject: tower
one_liner: The plane volume elements $\omega_j = e_j f_j$ square to one, anticommute with their own plane, commute with all other generators and with each other, and their product $\Omega_k$ squares to one, commutes with the ground generators and anticommutes with every plane generator.

title: The ascent renders the grade involution inner
subject: completion
one_liner: In the one-generator ascent, conjugation by the adjoined generator $\nu$ is the grade involution on $A$, exchanging the projectors $\varepsilon_\pm$, so either one generates the whole algebra.

title: Decomposition and commutation
subject: completion
one_liner:
The one-generator ascent splits as $B_\gamma = A \oplus A
u$ with $
u a = \hat a\, 
u$, and $
u^{-1} = \gamma
u$ when $\gamma = \pm 1$.

title: Density
subject: completion
one_liner: The lifted invertible points $[X(x)]$ with $Q(x) \neq 0$ are dense in the quadric $\mathcal{Q}$.

title: Matrix units, and the Peirce isomorphism
subject: completion
one_liner: The projectors $\varepsilon_\pm$ and the adjoined generator $\nu$ form a full system of $2 \times 2$ matrix units, so $B_\gamma \cong \Mat_2(E_{11} B_\gamma E_{11})$.

title: Minimality
subject: completion
one_liner: Every null-lift completion adjoins directions of both signs, so the minimal completion is the hyperbolic-plane ascent $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$, unique up to isometry, with increment $(+1,+1)$.

title: No-go at the level of elements
subject: zero-divisors
one_liner: In mixed signature with $n \geq 3$, no assignment of von Neumann pseudo-inverses to null vectors, valued in the Clifford algebra of any extension, is equivariant even under $\Spin^0(p,q)$.

title: Rule 1 is Morita-trivial
subject: completion
one_liner: Rule 1 gives $\Cl(p+1, q+1) \cong \Mat_2(\Cl(p,q))$ with the adjoined ladder pair as off-diagonal matrix units, so it preserves the Morita class, the Wedderburn type and the clock residue $p - q \pmod 8$.

title: Splitting along a hyperbolic plane
subject: zero-divisors
one_liner: Along a hyperbolic plane spanned by $(v, w_0)$, every element of $\Cl(H_0 \perp U')$ expands uniquely as $\alpha + v\beta + w_0\gamma + v w_0\delta$ with coefficients in $\Cl(U')$, and left multiplication by $v$ is injective on $\Cl(U')$.

title: Totality
subject: completion
one_liner: On the quadric of the completion, $\iota[N] = [e_+ N e_+]$ is a total continuous involution that equals the reciprocal $x \mapsto x/Q(x)$ on invertible vectors and sends each $x_0$ with $Q(x_0) = 0$ to $[x_0 + \frac12 \nInf]$, and it is the only such continuous extension.
